title: heilbronn-convex-3-8
abstract:
For n = 3 through n = 8, this formalization determines the supremal minimum triangle area among n indexed planar points whose own convex hull has Lebesgue area one. It proves a pointwise upper bound, attainment, and the exact value for every n in that range. The values are 1, 1/2, (5-sqrt(5))/10, 1/6, 1/9, and, at n = 8, the unique root in (79/1000, 81/1000) of 2060x^5 - 2332x^4 + 1064x^3 - 240x^2 + 26x - 1.
For n = 3, 4, 5, 6, and 8 it also proves pairwise uniqueness of optimizers modulo arbitrary relabeling and arbitrary nonsingular affine transformations. Uniqueness is false at n = 7; instead, an explicit real family is proved to attain throughout its full parameter interval and to exhaust all unit-hull optimizers up to the same equivalence. A real subinterval is pairwise inequivalent, exhibiting a continuum-parameterized set of optimizer orbits; an explicit countable subfamily is retained too.
The n = 3 and n = 4 cases are elementary folklore. The sharp n = 6 and n = 7 values were published by Dress-Yang-Zeng and Yang-Zeng, respectively; the Lean developments here independently reprove those results rather than formalizing the published arguments. The full n = 5 result, the explicit n = 7 family and optimizer classification, and the exact n = 8 result and optimizer classification are first presented in this development. The scoped search described below located prior candidate records but no published full n = 5 proof, no prior exhaustive n = 7 optimizer classification, and no published n = 8 proof. This is not an absolute priority claim. These results are intended for researchers in discrete and computational geometry studying extremal configurations, exact geometric bounds, and formalized combinatorial geometry.
